data.gender_notes: Mausoof is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word ‘mawsuf’ meaning fortified or protected. In Islamic history, it is believed that Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) was given the title ‘Ma'soom’ (impeccable) due to his unwavering commitment to Allah and His teachings. The name Mausoof carries the meaning “Fortified, Strong” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Mausoof usually hope their child will grow to embody fortified, strong and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes strength in faith and resilience in the face of adversity.
data.etymology: Mausoof belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Fortified, Strong.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mausoof total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

This name reflects the importance of good character and attributes in Islam. Historically, it has been used to denote individuals with notable qualities. The name Mausoof is associated with positive personality traits such as being descriptive, articulate, and having a strong sense of identity. Across Muslim cultures, it is used to signify a person with praiseworthy attributes.
